patches.rationale: Many PDSs state a single default excess per claim/event even when optional excesses also exist. The Cover‑More Corporate PDS specifies a fixed $60 per event excess (with age-based variations). Capturing a standard/base excess improves cross‑insurer comparison beyond free‑text excess notes.
patches.description: Standard base policy excess per claim/event (AUD) where a fixed default excess applies. Do not include optional buy‑down/buy‑up variants here; capture those in excess_options_aud. Note any age or section-specific overrides under special_excesses.

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: “The excess applies per event… the claimant is required to pay the first $60 arising from any one event on each journey in respect of Sections 1, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10… (Policy conditions, p15; section 1 on p19).”

patches.rationale: Australian domestic policies generally exclude medical treatment/evacuation in Australia due to Medicare legislation; corporate policies also state this. A simple boolean enables consistent flagging across domestic and business products.
patches.description: True if the policy explicitly excludes medical treatment and evacuation costs incurred in Australia (e.g., due to Medicare/PHI legislation). Capture supporting wording in general_exclusions_summary.

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: “We don’t cover medical treatment or evacuation costs under this policy… These expenses are covered in Australia from Medicare or your private health insurer.” (p22, p28).
“Medical and hospital cover in Australia – We will not pay any benefit… if… would result in us contravening the Health Insurance Act… Private Health Insurance Act… National Health Act.” (p4).

patches.rationale: Corporate annual multi‑trip policies often specify a per‑journey cap. Cover‑More Corporate sets a 6‑month maximum per journey. Extending applies_to to business improves reuse for corporate AMT products.
patches.description: Maximum journey duration allowed per trip for Annual Multi-Trip (days).

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: “period of insurance… ceasing at… the completion of 6 months from the commencement of each journey, whichever occurs first.” (p18).

patches.rationale: Corporate travel policies frequently allow limited personal/leisure travel in conjunction with business trips; limits and eligibility (e.g., executives) vary by insurer. Capturing this allowance aids corporate comparisons.
patches.description: Leisure/holiday travel allowance under a corporate policy, including who qualifies and maximum duration (e.g., ‘Employees: up to 4 weeks when combined with a business trip; Directors/CEO/CFO/COO: up to 6 weeks combined plus up to 6 weeks independent leisure’).

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: Employees: ‘includes up to 4 weeks of leisure/holiday travel incorporated in the same business trip.’ Executives (CEO/CFO/COO/Director): ‘includes up to 6 weeks… incorporated in the same business trip… Also… up to 6 weeks of leisure/holiday travel independent of a business trip.’ (pp3,16).

patches.rationale: Identity theft appears as a distinct, named benefit in corporate and some retail policies. Adding a dedicated coverage category improves normalisation for benefits mapping.
patches.description: Add a new coverage category for identity theft related legal and remediation costs.

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: Benefits table item 19: ‘Identity theft protection’ ($10,000–$15,000). Section 19 details scope (p34).

patches.rationale: Corporate policies commonly include an extra‑territorial workers’ compensation extension. A dedicated category improves clarity over placing it generically under business benefits.
patches.description: Add a coverage category for extra‑territorial workers’ compensation extensions (top‑ups to statutory workers’ comp while on business travel).

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: Benefits table item 18: ‘Extra territorial workers compensation’ ($500,000–$1,000,000). Section 18 outlines terms (p34).

patches.rationale: Security/political evacuation and disaster evacuation benefits are present in corporate policies and sometimes as retail add‑ons. A distinct category improves comparability and avoids overloading ‘additional expenses’.
patches.description: Add a coverage category for security, political unrest and disaster evacuation (costs to evacuate to safety or home when advised due to unrest or declared disasters).

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: Extras Section 26: ‘Political unrest and disaster evacuation’ ($25,000–$50,000). (p36).
